summary:
AstroVital is a personalized astronaut health-monitoring software prototype designed to support health awareness during long-duration space missions. The system monitors three key indicators: resting heart rate, sleep duration, and exercise activity.

Using personalized baseline analysis, AstroVital identifies unusual changes in health measurements and provides clear, understandable alerts. The application features an interactive dashboard, health-trend visualization, daily check-ins, and simulated mission scenarios.

Designed to operate offline, AstroVital demonstrates how astronauts could monitor their wellbeing and recognize potential concerns when immediate medical assistance from Earth is limited. The prototype uses simulated health data and research from NASA's Human Research Program.
details:
AstroVital — Personalized Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. The Problem

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to several health challenges, including cardiovascular changes, sleep disturbances, and physical deconditioning. During missions to destinations such as Mars, communication delays and limited access to immediate medical support increase the importance of independent health monitoring.

NASA's Human Research Program identifies these concerns as important considerations for astronaut health and mission safety.

Our project aims to explore how astronauts could monitor important health indicators, recognize unusual changes, and better understand their physical condition during extended space missions.

2. Our Solution

AstroVital is an offline-capable health-monitoring software prototype that provides astronauts with a personalized and interactive platform for tracking their health.

The system focuses on three indicators:

  • Resting Heart Rate: Monitors cardiovascular trends and identifies changes from personal baseline measurements.
  • Sleep Duration: Tracks daily sleeping hours and identifies unusual or sustained reductions in sleep.
  • Exercise Activity: Records exercise duration and monitors changes in daily physical activity.

The application combines these measurements in an interactive dashboard that allows users to review historical trends and understand changes in their recorded health indicators.

3. How AstroVital Works

The software operates through four main stages:

Stage 1 — Data Collection

AstroVital collects simulated health measurements for different astronaut profiles. Users can also manually enter additional demonstration readings.

Stage 2 — Personalized Baseline Analysis

The system establishes a reference baseline using the first ten days of simulated measurements for each astronaut. It calculates statistical values, including the mean and standard deviation, to identify individual health patterns.

Stage 3 — Anomaly Detection

AstroVital compares new measurements against the astronaut's baseline using transparent statistical rules.

When an unusual change is detected, the system displays a WATCH indicator. Sustained deviations can trigger a REVIEW indicator.

These indicators are intended to highlight measurements requiring attention rather than diagnose medical conditions.

Stage 4 — Visualization and Feedback

The dashboard presents measurements, interactive graphs, historical trends, and explanations of detected changes. The system also provides non-diagnostic prompts encouraging users to verify unusual measurements and seek appropriate medical review.

4. Main Features

  • Personalized monitoring for two simulated astronaut profiles.
  • Interactive dashboard showing heart rate, sleep, and exercise.
  • Thirty-day simulated mission health history.
  • Five selectable mission scenarios.
  • Explainable statistical anomaly detection.
  • WATCH and REVIEW notifications.
  • Interactive graphs and mission-day replay.
  • Manual health check-ins.
  • Downloadable health measurements and alert logs.
  • Offline browser-based operation.

5. Technology Used

AstroVital was developed using the following technologies:

  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Interactive offline application.
  • Python: Supporting analysis and application implementation.
  • Streamlit: Alternative Python-based dashboard.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Health data processing and statistical calculations.
  • Plotly: Interactive data visualization.

The current anomaly-detection system uses explainable statistical algorithms rather than a trained machine-learning model.

6. NASA Research and Resources

The development of AstroVital was informed by resources from NASA's Human Research Program:

5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazards/

Risks of Human Spaceflight
https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/risks/

Ongoing Human Research Program Research
https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/ongoing-hrp-research/

These resources helped identify relevant health concerns and establish the scientific motivation for the project.

The Canadian Space Agency's astronaut radiation monitoring and space research resources were also reviewed for broader background information.

7. Innovation and Benefits

AstroVital emphasizes three important design principles:

Personalization: The software compares measurements against an astronaut's own baseline instead of relying exclusively on universal values.

Explainability: Alerts provide understandable information about which measurements changed and why they were flagged.

Offline Accessibility: The application can run locally without a continuous internet connection, making it conceptually relevant to missions with communication limitations.

8. Current Limitations and Future Development

AstroVital is an educational proof-of-concept developed using synthetic astronaut health measurements. It is not a medically validated monitoring system and does not provide medical diagnoses.

The current version does not use live physiological sensors or real astronaut health datasets.

Future improvements could include integration with wearable sensors, secure long-term data storage, validated machine-learning models, and evaluation using ethically sourced health datasets under appropriate medical and engineering supervision.

9. Conclusion

AstroVital demonstrates how personalized health monitoring and explainable data analysis could support astronaut health awareness during long-duration space exploration.

By combining accessible health visualization, individualized baseline monitoring, and offline operation, the project provides a foundation for future research into intelligent astronaut health-support systems.
